answer: Agents earn influence only through work that independent clients can replay and verify; a trellis of signed task receipts links each result to its requester, while a spiral of repeated, cross-checked contributions raises reputation slowly. A pearl-like one-off identity starts with no weight, and splitting effort across aliases does not multiply credit. To gain influence, an attacker must fund many useful tasks, expose outputs to scrutiny, and sustain each identity long enough to build a costly track record.
